chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about what expiates from the oaths. He said: 'That which was obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, there is no expiation upon you. And that which was not obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, then upon you is the expiation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiating an oath not to do something obligatory versus something non-obligatory?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through the chain of Zurarah, this hadith clarifies the juristic principle that oaths regarding obligatory duties do not incur expiation when fulfilled, whereas oaths against non-obligatory acts do. This distinction highlights the Shia view that breaking a vow to abstain from a recommended or neutral act constitutes a violation requiring atonement, reinforcing the spiritual weight of voluntary commitments.
